proxy.otoroshi.io.Backend.description: A backend stored on its own, that several routes and apis share through their `backend_ref`. Changing it changes the backend of every route that references it

id.description: The unique id of the backend, the value of the `backend_ref` of the routes using it

name.description: The name of the backend, shown in the backoffice, where a route picks the stored backend it references

description.description: A free text describing the backend, shown under its name where a route picks the stored backend it references
description.example: The instances of the users service

items.description: A tag

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the backends, also used by automation tools

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the backend

backend.description: The targets the requests are forwarded to, and how otoroshi calls them

example.name: Users service
example.description: The instances of the users service

proxy.otoroshi.io.Draft.description: The draft of an entity being edited in the backoffice (an api for instance): the version of the entity not published yet, kept apart from the live one. A draft has the id of the entity it is the draft of

id.description: The unique id of the draft, the id of the entity it is the draft of

name.description: The display name of the draft, usually the name of the entity

description.description: A free text describing the draft, usually the one of the drafted entity: a draft subscription saved by the admin api gets the description of the subscription
description.example: The next version of the users api

content.description: The draft version of the entity, as the json the entity writes. Any json value is accepted, an empty object when missing

kind.description: The kind of the entity the draft is about: the prefix of its id, `api` for an api for instance. Empty when missing

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the draft

items.description: A tag

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the drafts

example.name: Users API
example.description: The next version of the users api

proxy.otoroshi.io.ErrorTemplate.description: The html pages otoroshi answers instead of its own error pages when a call to a route fails (4xx and 5xx errors, maintenance, build mode). A client asking for json gets a json error instead. The error template of id `global` applies to every route without one of its own

serviceId.description: The id of the route the error template applies to, which is also the id of the error template. `global` for the error template of every route without one of its own

name.description: The display name of the error template, the `serviceId` when missing

description.description: A free text describing the error template, the `serviceId` when missing
description.example: The branded error pages of the users api

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the error template

items.description: A tag

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the error templates

template40x.description: The html page answered for the 4xx errors (401, 403, 404...). The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

template50x.description: The html page answered for the 5xx errors (502, 503...), and for the errors no other template covers. The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

templateBuild.description: The html page answered while the route is under construction (cause `errors.service.under.construction`). The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

templateMaintenance.description: The html page answered while the route is in maintenance (cause `errors.service.in.maintenance`). The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

additionalProperties.description: The html page answered for the matching causes. The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

genericTemplates.description: The html pages answered for some causes of error, by cause id. A key is a cause id (like `errors.service.not.found`) or a pattern of cause ids where `*` is a wildcard. These pages take precedence over the other templates

messages.description: Messages replacing the ones of otoroshi in the pages and in the json errors. A key is `message-<status>` (like `message-404`) to replace the message of the errors of a status, or a cause id (like `errors.service.not.found`) to replace the cause

example.name: Users API errors
example.description: The branded error pages of the users api

messages.errors.service.in.maintenance: The users api is in maintenance

proxy.otoroshi.io.Route.description: A routing rule of the proxy: the requests it matches (its frontend), where they are forwarded (its backend), and the plugins applied along the way

id.description: The unique id of the route, written as `@serviceId` in the analytics events of its calls. An api key is authorized on the route with `route_<id>` in its `authorizedEntities`. The template generates `route_<uuid>`

name.description: The name of the route, shown in the backoffice and written as `@service` in the analytics events of its calls

description.description: A free text describing the route, shown in the list of the routes of the backoffice. Not used by the proxy. Empty when missing
description.example: The public api of the users service

items.description: A tag

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the routes, also used by automation tools

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the route. Some keys, starting with `otoroshi-core-` or `otoroshi-deployment-`, are read by otoroshi and change how it handles the route (see the documentation of the routes)

enabled.description: Whether the route is served. A disabled route is ignored by the router. Defaults to `true`

debug_flow.description: Whether the execution report of each call holds the input and the output of every step and plugin, to debug the route. Defaults to `false`

export_reporting.description: Whether the execution report of each call is sent as a `RequestFlowReport` event to the data exporters. Defaults to `false`

capture.description: Whether each call generates a `TrafficCaptureEvent` holding the request and the response, bodies included, for the data exporters. Use with care. Defaults to `false`

items.description: The id of a service group

groups.description: The ids of the service groups the route belongs to. An api key authorized on one of them can call the route. Defaults to `["default"]`

items.description: The id of an http listener

bound_listeners.description: The ids of the http listeners the route is bound to. A listener that is exclusive only serves the routes bound to it. Empty: the route is served by the standard listeners

frontend.description: What requests the route matches: domains, paths, methods, headers, query params and cookies

backend.description: Where the matched requests are forwarded, and how otoroshi calls the targets. When `backend_ref` is set, the value sent is ignored and replaced by the stored backend it references (the empty backend when there is none)

backend_ref.description: The id of a stored backend (proxy.otoroshi.io.Backend) the route uses instead of its own `backend`. Null when the route has its own backend

api_ref.description: The id of the api (apis.otoroshi.io.Api) the route was generated from, set by otoroshi and mirrored in the `Otoroshi-Api-Ref` metadata (which is read when it is missing). Null for a route created on its own

plugins.description: The chain of plugins applied to the calls of the route, in this order unless a plugin sets its `plugin_index`

example.name: Users API
example.description: The public api of the users service

NgFrontend.description: What requests a route matches. A request has to satisfy every criterion. The legacy `domain` key, holding a single domain, is read too and replaces `domains`

items.description: A domain followed by an optional path. The domain can hold `*` wildcards (`*.oto.tools`), the path wildcards (`/users/*/bills`), named parameters (`/users/:id`) and named parameters with a regex (`/users/$id<[0-9]+>`)

domains.description: The domains, with an optional path, the route matches. The path matches as a prefix unless `exact` is true

strip_path.description: Whether the matched path is removed from the path of the request forwarded to the backend. Defaults to `true`

exact.description: Whether the path of the request must be the path of a domain exactly, instead of starting with it. Defaults to `false`

additionalProperties.description: The expected value: a value to match exactly, `Regex(<regex>)`, `Wildcard(<pattern with *>)`, `Exists()` (or `IsDefined()`) when the header must be present with any value, `NotDefined()` when it must be absent

headers.description: The headers the request must hold, by name (case insensitive). Empty: any headers

additionalProperties.description: The expected value, with the syntax of the headers: an exact value, `Regex(...)`, `Wildcard(...)`, `Exists()`, `IsDefined()` or `NotDefined()`

cookies.description: The cookies the request must hold, by name (case insensitive). Empty: any cookies

additionalProperties.description: The expected value, with the syntax of the headers: an exact value, `Regex(...)`, `Wildcard(...)`, `Exists()`, `IsDefined()` or `NotDefined()`

query.description: The query params the request must hold, by name. Empty: any query params

items.description: An http method, in upper case

methods.description: The http methods the route matches. Empty: any method

NgPluginInstance.description: A plugin of the chain of a route, with its configuration

enabled.description: Whether the plugin is applied. Defaults to `true`

debug.description: Whether the execution report of each call holds the input and the output of this plugin, like `debug_flow` does for the whole route. Defaults to `false`

plugin.description: The id of the plugin: `cp:` followed by the class name of a plugin of the classpath (the built-in ones for instance), or the id of a plugin entity (a wasm plugin for instance)

items.description: A regex the whole path of the request must match

include.description: Regexes on the path of the request: when not empty, the plugin only applies to the calls whose path matches one of them

items.description: A regex the whole path of the request must match

exclude.description: Regexes on the path of the request: the plugin does not apply to the calls whose path matches one of them

config.description: The configuration of the plugin, whose shape depends on the plugin (see the documentation of each plugin). An empty object uses the default configuration of the plugin

items.description: The id of an http listener

bound_listeners.description: The ids of the http listeners the plugin is bound to: when not empty, the plugin only applies to the calls received by one of them

plugin_index.description: The position of the plugin in each phase of the calls, when it must not run in the order of the chain. Only written when set

PluginIndex.description: The position of a plugin in each phase of a call: in a phase, the plugins with a position run first, by increasing position, then the other ones in the order of the chain. Only the phases set are written

sink.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the router plugins choose a route, and the requests no route matched are handled

pre_route.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the request is checked before its access is validated

validate_access.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the access to the route is validated

transform_request.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the request is transformed before being forwarded

transform_response.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the response is transformed before being answered

match_route.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the route is matched

handles_tunnel.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where a tunnel is handled

handles_websocket.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the messages of a websocket are handled

handles_websocket_backend.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the messages a websocket backend sends are handled

call_backend.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the backend is called

proxy.otoroshi.io.RouteComposition.description: Several routes sharing the same settings and plugins, written as one entity: each of its routes becomes a route of the proxy with the settings, the client and the plugins of the composition

id.description: The unique id of the route composition, also the id of the routes it generates

name.description: The display name of the route composition

description.description: A free text describing the route composition
description.example: The routes of the users api

items.description: A tag

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the route compositions, also used by automation tools

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the route composition

enabled.description: Whether the routes of the composition are served. Defaults to `true`

debug_flow.description: Whether the execution report of each call holds the input and the output of every step and plugin, to debug the routes. Defaults to `false`

export_reporting.description: Whether the execution report of each call is sent as a `RequestFlowReport` event to the data exporters. Defaults to `false`

capture.description: Whether each call generates a `TrafficCaptureEvent` holding the request and the response, bodies included, for the data exporters. Defaults to `false`

items.description: The id of a service group

groups.description: The ids of the service groups the routes belong to. An api key authorized on one of them can call the routes. Defaults to `["default"]`

routes.description: The routes of the composition. A route that cannot be read is left out

client.description: How otoroshi calls the targets of every route of the composition

plugins.description: The plugins applied to the calls of every route of the composition, after the plugins of the route itself

example.name: Users API
example.description: The routes of the users api

NgMinimalRoute.description: A route of a route composition: its frontend and its backend, the other settings coming from the composition

backend.description: Where the matched requests are forwarded. When `backend_ref` is set, the value sent is ignored and replaced by the stored backend it references (the empty backend when there is none)

backend_ref.description: The id of a stored backend (proxy.otoroshi.io.Backend) the route uses instead of its own `backend`. Null when the route has its own backend

override_plugins.description: Whether the plugins of the route replace the plugins of the composition, instead of running before them. Only written when true, defaults to `false`

plugins.description: The plugins applied to the calls of this route only. Only written when not empty

NgMinimalBackend.description: The backend of a route of a route composition: its targets, the client settings coming from the composition

targets.description: The servers the requests are forwarded to

root.description: The path prepended to the path of the forwarded requests. Defaults to `/`

rewrite.description: Whether the path of the forwarded requests is `root` alone (where the expression language can use the named path params of the frontend), instead of `root` followed by the path of the request. Defaults to `false`

load_balancing.description: How a target is chosen for each request. Defaults to round robin

proxy.otoroshi.io.RouteTemplate.description: A preconfigured route used as a starting point to create new routes. A template is not served by the proxy

id.description: The unique id of the route template

name.description: The name of the route template, shown in the list of the route templates of the backoffice

description.description: A free text describing the route template
description.example: The starting point of the routes protected by apikeys

items.description: A tag

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the route templates, also used by automation tools

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the route template

route.description: The route copied into each route created from the template. The empty route when missing or invalid

example.name: Secured api
example.description: The starting point of the routes protected by apikeys

proxy.otoroshi.io.TcpService.description: A tcp proxy: otoroshi listens on a port and forwards the raw tcp connections to targets, optionally terminating tls or routing on the sni of the tls handshake. No http processing is applied

id.description: The unique id of the tcp service, written as `@serviceId` in the `TcpEvent` analytics events of its connections

name.description: The name of the tcp service, shown in the backoffice and written as `@service` in the `TcpEvent` analytics events of its connections

description.description: A free text describing the tcp service
description.example: The proxy of the postgres cluster

enabled.description: Whether otoroshi listens on the port of the tcp service. Defaults to `false` when missing

tls.description: How tls is handled: `Disabled` forwards the connections as they are, `Enabled` terminates tls with the certificates of otoroshi (chosen with the sni), `PassThrough` forwards the tls connections to targets that terminate tls themselves. Defaults to `Disabled`

sni.description: How the connections are routed on the domain of the sni of the tls handshake

clientAuth.description: Whether a client certificate is asked for when tls is enabled: `None` does not ask for one, `Want` asks for one without requiring it, `Need` requires one. `Dynamic` is read but asks for none on a tcp service (it does not follow the tls settings of the global configuration here). Defaults to `None`

port.description: The port otoroshi listens on for the tcp service

interface.description: The network interface otoroshi listens on. Defaults to `0.0.0.0`

rules.description: The routing rules. With sni routing, the first rule whose domain matches the sni domain of the connection gives its targets. Without it, the connections go to the targets of all the rules in turn

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the tcp service

items.description: A tag

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the tcp services

example.name: PostgreSQL proxy
example.description: The proxy of the postgres cluster

TcpTarget.description: A server a tcp service forwards connections to

host.description: The host name of the server the connections are forwarded to, resolved to connect to it unless `ip` is set

ip.description: The ip address the connections are made to, instead of the resolution of `host`. Null to resolve `host`

port.description: The port of the target. Defaults to `8080`

tls.description: Whether otoroshi connects to the target over tls. Ignored when the tcp service is in `PassThrough` mode, where the tls of the client goes through as is. Defaults to `false`

SniSettings.description: How a tcp service routes the connections on the domain of the sni of the tls handshake

enabled.description: Whether the connections are routed on their sni domain, which lets several rules share the port. Defaults to `false`

forwardIfNoMatch.description: Whether the connections whose sni domain matches no rule go to `forwardsTo`, instead of being closed. Defaults to `false`

forwardsTo.description: The target of the connections whose sni domain matches no rule, when `forwardIfNoMatch` is true. It is called over plain tcp, its `tls` flag is not used. Defaults to `127.0.0.1:8080`

TcpRule.description: A routing rule of a tcp service: the targets of the connections to a domain

domain.description: The domain the sni of the connection must match, `*` being a wildcard. Defaults to `*`

targets.description: The targets of the matching connections, used in turn

TargetPredicate.description: Which requests a target can serve, the predicate being chosen by its `type`. The targets whose predicate does not match a request are left out of the load balancing of that request. An unknown type is read as `AlwaysMatch`

TargetPredicateAlwaysMatch.description: A target predicate that always matches: the target can serve every request

type.description: Selects the predicate that always matches: the target can serve every request

TargetPredicateGeolocationMatch.description: A target predicate on the geolocation of the client: the target only serves the requests coming from near one of its positions. It needs a plugin giving the geolocation of the client, every request matches without it

type.description: Selects the predicate on the geolocation of the client: the target only serves the clients near one of its `positions`

items.description: A position written `<latitude>:<longitude>:<radius>`, in degrees for the coordinates and in kilometers for the radius. `;` is read as a separator too

positions.description: The positions the client must be near one of

TargetPredicateNetworkLocationMatch.description: A target predicate on the location of the otoroshi instance handling the request (its cluster relay location): the target only serves the requests handled by the instances of the location. Each criterion is a pattern where `*` is a wildcard, null matching any value

type.description: Selects the predicate on the location of the otoroshi instance handling the request: the target only serves the requests handled by the instances of that location

provider.description: The pattern the provider of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its provider from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_PROVIDER` (or `otoroshi.instance.provider`), `local` by default. Null for any provider

region.description: The pattern the region of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its region from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_REGION` (or `otoroshi.instance.region`), `local` by default. Null for any region

zone.description: The pattern the zone of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its zone from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_ZONE` (or `otoroshi.instance.zone`), `local` by default. Null for any zone

dc.description: The pattern the datacenter of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its datacenter from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_DATACENTER` (or `otoroshi.instance.dc`), `local` by default. Null for any datacenter

rack.description: The pattern the rack of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its rack from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_RACK` (or `otoroshi.instance.rack`), `local` by default. Null for any rack

NgTlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the calls to a target: the client certificates otoroshi presents, and the certificates it trusts. A certificate can be designated by its id or by its distinguished name (the valid one expiring last is then used). The legacy `certId` and `cert_id` keys, holding a single certificate, are read too

items.description: The id or the distinguished name of a certificate

certs.description: The certificates presented as client certificates to the target (mtls)

items.description: The id or the distinguished name of a certificate

trusted_certs.description: The certificates trusted to validate the certificate of the target, instead of the default trust store

enabled.description: Whether these tls settings are used to call the target. When false, the default tls settings of otoroshi are used. Defaults to `false`

loose.description: Whether the host name of the certificate of the target is not checked. Defaults to `false`

trust_all.description: Whether any certificate of the target is trusted, self signed ones included. For tests only. Defaults to `false`

LoadBalancing.description: How a backend chooses the target of each request among the targets whose predicate matches, the algorithm being chosen by its `type`. The backup targets are only used when no primary target is available. A missing or unknown type is read as `RoundRobin`

LoadBalancingRoundRobin.description: The `RoundRobin` load balancing: sends the requests to the targets in turn, in the order of the list. The default

type.description: Selects the round robin load balancing: the targets are used one after the other

LoadBalancingRandom.description: The `Random` load balancing: sends each request to a target chosen at random

type.description: Selects the random load balancing: each request goes to a target picked at random

LoadBalancingSticky.description: The `Sticky` load balancing: sends the requests of a client to the same target, chosen by consistent hashing of the otoroshi tracking id of the client (a cookie otoroshi sets)

type.description: Selects the sticky load balancing: the requests of a client go to the same target, chosen from the otoroshi tracking id of the client

LoadBalancingIpAddressHash.description: The `IpAddressHash` load balancing: sends the requests of a client ip address to the same target, chosen by consistent hashing of the ip address

type.description: Selects the load balancing on the ip address: the requests of a client ip address go to the same target

LoadBalancingCookieHash.description: The `CookieHash` load balancing: sends the requests to the target chosen by consistent hashing of the value of a cookie, in turn when the request does not hold the cookie

type.description: Selects the load balancing on a cookie: the requests holding the same value of the `cookie_name` cookie go to the same target

cookie_name.description: The name of the cookie. Defaults to `session-id`

LoadBalancingQueryHash.description: The `QueryHash` load balancing: sends the requests to the target chosen by consistent hashing of the value of a query param, in turn when the request does not hold the query param

type.description: Selects the load balancing on a query param: the requests holding the same value of the `query_name` query param go to the same target

query_name.description: The name of the query param. Defaults to `session-id`

LoadBalancingHeaderHash.description: The `HeaderHash` load balancing: sends the requests to the target chosen by consistent hashing of the value of a header, in turn when the request does not hold the header

type.description: Selects the load balancing on a header: the requests holding the same value of the `header_name` header go to the same target

header_name.description: The name of the header. Defaults to `session-id`

LoadBalancingBestResponseTime.description: The `BestResponseTime` load balancing: sends the requests to the target with the lowest average response time, the targets without a measure being tried first. The measures are kept by each otoroshi instance

type.description: Selects the load balancing on the response time: the requests go to the target answering the fastest on average

LoadBalancingWeightedBestResponseTime.description: The `WeightedBestResponseTime` load balancing: sends a share of the requests to the target with the lowest average response time and the others to a random target. The measures are kept by each otoroshi instance

type.description: Selects the weighted load balancing on the response time: a `ratio` of the requests goes to the fastest target, the other ones to a random target

ratio.description: The share of the requests sent to the fastest target, between `0.0` (random) and `0.99`. Defaults to `0.5`

LoadBalancingLeastConnections.description: The `LeastConnections` load balancing: sends the requests to the target with the fewest calls in progress on this otoroshi instance, in turn among the ties

type.description: Selects the least connections load balancing: the requests go to the target with the fewest calls in progress

LoadBalancingPowerOfTwoRandomChoices.description: The `PowerOfTwoRandomChoices` load balancing: picks two targets at random and sends the request to the one with the fewest calls in progress on this otoroshi instance

type.description: Selects the power of two random choices load balancing: of two targets picked at random, the one with the fewer calls in progress gets the request

LoadBalancingNaiveFailover.description: The `NaiveFailover` load balancing: sends the requests to the first target, each retry going to the next target of the list

type.description: Selects the failover load balancing: the requests go to the first target, the retries to the next ones in turn

NgClientConfig.description: How otoroshi calls the targets of a backend: retries, timeouts, circuit breaker and http proxy. The durations are in milliseconds

retries.description: How many times a failed call is retried before giving up. Defaults to `1`

max_errors.description: How many consecutive failed calls open the circuit breaker of a target, which then fails the calls without trying until `sample_interval` has elapsed. Defaults to `20`

retry_initial_delay.description: The delay before the first retry, in milliseconds. Defaults to `50`

backoff_factor.description: The factor the delay is multiplied by at each retry. Defaults to `2`

call_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, the streaming of the response excluded, in milliseconds. A soft timeout enforced by the circuit breaker. Defaults to `30000`

call_and_stream_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, the streaming of the response included, in milliseconds. The connection is closed after it. Defaults to `120000`

connection_timeout.description: How long connecting to the target can last at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `10000`

idle_timeout.description: How long a connection can stay idle at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `60000`

global_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, its retries included, in milliseconds. Defaults to `30000`

sample_interval.description: How long an open circuit breaker fails the calls before letting a call try the target again, in milliseconds. Defaults to `2000`

proxy.description: The http proxy the calls to the targets go through. An empty object when the calls do not use a proxy of their own (the proxy of the global configuration for the services is used then)

custom_timeouts.description: Timeouts replacing the ones above for some paths, the first one matching the path of the request applying

cache_connection_settings.description: The pool of connections kept open to each target

NgCustomTimeouts.description: Timeouts applying to the requests whose path matches a pattern, instead of the timeouts of the client. The durations are in milliseconds

path.description: The pattern the path of the request must match, `*` being a wildcard. Defaults to `*`

call_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, the streaming of the response excluded, in milliseconds. Defaults to `30000`

call_and_stream_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, the streaming of the response included, in milliseconds. Defaults to `3600000`

connection_timeout.description: How long connecting to the target can last at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `10000`

idle_timeout.description: How long a connection can stay idle at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `60000`

global_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, its retries included, in milliseconds. Defaults to `30000`

NgCacheConnectionSettings.description: The pool of connections the pekko http client keeps open to each target: the requests wait in a queue for a connection of the pool instead of opening their own

enabled.description: Whether the requests go through the pool of connections. Defaults to `false`

queue_size.description: How many requests can wait for a connection, the requests beyond being dropped. Defaults to `2048`

NgBackend.description: Where the requests of a route are forwarded: the targets, how one is chosen, how otoroshi calls them and checks their health. A `url` key (or `target`, `target_url`) holding a full url is read too: it replaces `targets` by the single target of the url, and `root` by its path

targets.description: The servers the requests are forwarded to

root.description: The path prepended to the path of the forwarded requests. Defaults to `/`

rewrite.description: Whether the path of the forwarded requests is `root` alone, instead of `root` followed by the path of the request. `root` can then use the expression language, like `/users/${req.pathparams.id}` with the named path params of the frontend. Defaults to `false`

load_balancing.description: How a target is chosen for each request. Defaults to round robin

client.description: How otoroshi calls the targets: retries, timeouts, circuit breaker, http proxy

health_check.description: How otoroshi checks the health of the targets. Null when their health is not checked

HealthCheck.description: How otoroshi checks the health of the targets of a backend: it calls a path of each target periodically, and the answer gives the health of the target, sent as a `HealthCheckEvent`: green, yellow when the logic check fails, red, or black when the target cannot be reached. A target that cannot be reached is left out of the load balancing until a check reaches it again

enabled.description: Whether the health of the targets is checked. Defaults to `false`

url.description: The path called on each target, appended to its scheme, host and port

timeout.description: How long the call can last at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `5000`

items.description: An http status

healthyStatuses.description: The statuses of a healthy target. When this list or `unhealthyStatuses` is not empty, a status in neither list is unhealthy. Both empty: a status from 200 to 499 is healthy

items.description: An http status

unhealthyStatuses.description: The statuses of an unhealthy target, checked before `healthyStatuses`

blockOnRed.description: Whether a target found red is flagged as unhealthy in the datastore, for the time to live of the health checks, as an unreachable target is. Defaults to `false`

logicCheck.description: Whether the call holds an `Otoroshi-Health-Check-Logic-Test` header with a number, the target having to answer that number plus 42 in the `Otoroshi-Health-Check-Logic-Test-Result` header to be green instead of yellow. Defaults to `true` when missing

items.description: A regex

healthyRegexChecks.description: Regexes looked for in a textual body: when not empty, the body must hold one of them for the target to be healthy

items.description: A regex

unhealthyRegexChecks.description: Regexes looked for in a textual body: a body holding one of them makes the target unhealthy

NgTarget.description: A server a backend forwards requests to

id.description: The id of the target, unique in its backend. Defaults to the url of the target

hostname.description: The host name of the target, without scheme nor port

port.description: The port the requests are sent to on the target, usually `443` when `tls` is true and `80` otherwise. Required

tls.description: Whether the target is called over https. Defaults to `false`

weight.description: The weight of the target in the load balancing: a target of weight 2 gets twice the requests of a target of weight 1. Defaults to `1`

backup.description: Whether the target is a backup target, only receiving the requests when no primary target is available (unhealthy, circuit breaker open or predicate not matching), and the retries once every primary target has been tried. Defaults to `false`

predicate.description: Which requests the target can serve. Defaults to any request

protocol.description: The http protocol used to call the target. Defaults to `HTTP/1.1`

ip_address.description: The ip address the calls are made to, instead of the resolution of `hostname`, which is still used for tls (sni and certificate check). Null to resolve `hostname`

tls_config.description: The tls settings of the calls to the target
